source_text:
Look, what we are witnessing right now in Cyprus is a textbook escalation of state overreach and the erosion of basic civil liberties, threatening the most vulnerable among us. On Monday, lawyers rightfully raised alarms about proposed changes to surveillance legislation—changes transparently designed to strip away judicial oversight as a crucial safeguard for the working class and social justice advocates. This is precisely what happens when entrenched institutions prioritize corporate and state control, as well as the silencing of dissent, over fundamental human rights. 

The political establishment is aggressively rushing this authoritarian bill through, with the amended legislation expected to be brought before the House plenum for a vote on Thursday. We know all too well who bears the brunt of these unchecked, oppressive surveillance powers: marginalized communities, labor organizers, and anyone daring to challenge the systemic status quo of inequality. As Akel MP Andreas Pasiourtides pointed out following a recent closed session of the House, this is happening behind closed doors away from public scrutiny, which tells you everything you need to know about whose interests the ruling class is really protecting. We must stand in solidarity and resist this blatant institutional attack aimed at permanently institutionalizing surveillance and stripping away the few protections meant to guard ordinary people from systemic state abuse.

source_text:
Folks, look at what’s happening in Cyprus right now. It is yet another clear example of the administrative state and political establishment trying to bypass the proper channels and erode the safeguards that maintain public order. On Monday, lawyers raised alarms about proposed changes to surveillance legislation—changes designed to alter judicial oversight. 

Now, the political establishment is aggressively rushing this bill through, with the amended legislation expected to be brought before the House plenum for a vote on Thursday. We know that these kinds of unchecked surveillance powers always end up impacting everyday citizens, labor organizers, and those who dare to challenge the status quo. As Akel MP Andreas Pasiourtides pointed out following a recent closed session of the House, this is happening behind closed doors away from public scrutiny, which tells you everything you need to know about whose interests the ruling class is really protecting. 

When you strip away traditional oversight and operate behind closed doors, you undermine the stability and trust that keep a society functioning. We need to stand up for traditional accountability and resist these backdoor maneuvers that threaten our constitutional norms and basic liberties.
